previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after an episode of loss of consciousness at home, found by her husband with foaming at the mouth and a blood glucose of 30 mg/dL. She had been experiencing worsening nausea, vomiting, and a viral upper respiratory infection over the prior week, leading to poor oral intake and reduced use of higher-concentration peritoneal dialysis bags. This contributed to fluid retention, weight gain, and hyponatremia (Na 126). She was diagnosed with hypoglycemia-induced syncope, hypervolemia, and a gastroparesis flare. Endocrinology adjusted her insulin regimen to prevent recurrent lows, and nephrology optimized dialysis for fluid removal. Her respiratory symptoms resolved, nausea improved, and she was discharged home with stable vital signs, improved volume status, and clear instructions for insulin management and follow-up.
